items.body_excerpt:
NRL Casualty Ward: McLean faces surgery; Double blow for Sharks
Panthers centre Casey McLean is set for surgery on a fractured hand and could be sidelined for up to four weeks.
McLean suffered the injury during Saturday's game against the Raiders in Mudgee and left the field with 20 minutes to play.
The Broncos were dealt a blow early in their clash with the Knights with Adam Reynolds leaving the field after a head knock.
The halfback tried to tackle Greg Marzhew front-on in the seventh minute of the clash at Suncorp Stadium but his head copped the winger's shoulder and he was deemed a Category 1 head knock and ruled out for the night.
Forward Xavier Willison left the field around the same time as Reynolds with a nasty gash to his leg. The Broncos initially hoped Willison would return but he did not get back on the field.
There was also drama in the warm-up for Brisbane with Payne Haas injuring his shoulder, however the prop received treatment and was able to take his place in the starting side.
The Broncos went into the match without Preston Riki , who has had surgery to repair a syndesmosis injury suffered in Round 21 against the Cowboys.
In Sunday's opening game, the Sharks lost both centre KL Iro and utility Sifa Talakai in their game against the Bunnies.
Iro failed his HIA in the first half, while Talakai came off with a biceps injury.
Following the match, coach Craig Fitzgibbon was hopeful Talakai's injury wasn't as bad as first feared.
"It's the top end, so it's not the bottom end, the bottom end means you're out, you're gone, it's the top end, so it's not as bad ... he's definitely done something to it, so we've got to work out what the time frame on that is, which was disappointing for us ..."
In Saturday's first game of the day, Titans halfback Zane Harrison came from the field late in the second half with a suspected hamstring injury.
Harrison had to be helped from the field by a trainer in the 75th minute as the Titans fell to a 42-6 loss.
"It's too early to tell," Titans coach Josh Hannay said when asked about the severity of the injury. "When I first saw it, the nature of it being his own doing, I was worried it was his knee.

The Warriors lost Demitric Vaimauga following captain's run with a ribs complaint, but he is only expected to miss one week.
The Dragons lost hard-working forward Toby Couchman to a failed HIA at WIN Stadium on Friday night.
Storm playmaker Jahrome Hughes was a late withdrawal from Friday night's clash against the Bulldogs due to hamstring tightness.
Centre Jack Howarth missed the match after injuring his shoulder at training while Harry Grant (hamstring) and Cameron Munster (knee) are also sidelined.
The Raiders suffered a blow ahead of their trip to Mudgee with gun centre Simi Sasagi ruled out with a hamstring injury.
Sasagi joined forward Noah Martin (quad) in the Raiders' casualty ward.
In Round 23's opening match, Roosters captain James Tedesco didn't play in the second half of his side's record 82-12 win over the Cowboys, sitting out the second half with ice on his left ankle.
However, the club weren't too concerned, with coach Trent Robinson saying Tedesco had informed him he was 'right to go' - but given the score, they opted to sit him out.
"There was a choice around his ankle, he was going okay, so I think he did it in the first five minutes," Robinson told reporters post-game.
"I saw him hobbling and ... he had a pretty good first half, and he said he was right to go, and I as a coach is sort of there going, 'I really want to set the tone again for the start of the second half', so you want to send your captain out there and the scoreline was what it was anyway, I decided to put Cody out there.

In this week's edition of the run home, Zero Tackle takes you through every game remaining, what each team needs to go right for their best-case scenarios, and where you can expect your side to be finished.
There has been just one change on the final predicted ladder, but the number of teams requiring miracles to play finals footy is growing.

As it stands, the Panthers are now the only team mathematically locked into the finals, although by the end of the coming week they may not be alone.

They start their final five weeks against the Bulldogs this week, looking for a slip up from the Panthers ahead of them to claim the minor premiership.

Late mail: De Groot joins bench against Warriors
Jaylan De Groot will join the Titans' bench for Saturday's clash against the Warriors at a sold out Cbus Super Stadium.
The 23-year-old is set to offer Josh Hannay outside back coverage after scoring a double at left centre last Sunday against the Dragons - AJ Brimson returning in that position after missing last week's win due to concussion.
Kurtis Morrin also returns from a leg infection as Gold Coast eye to notch up three wins on the trot for the first time in 2026; having won four of their past seven games - including two of their last three at home.
Hoping to avenge their Round 7 defeat in New Zealand, Hannay's men have won six of their last nine games against the Warriors, including four of their past six Trans-Tasman clashes at Robina.

Judiciary update: Georgia Hale
Georgia Hale has been charged by the match review committee following the Titans' Magic Round win against the Warriors on Sunday afternoon.
Placed on report in the 53rd minute of the game, the NRLW captain has been hit with a Grade 1 Contrary Contact charge on Kaiyah Atai, resulting in a one match suspension should she elect to take the early plea; although Hale does have the option to pay a $400 fine in lieu of the ban.
Should she fight the charge and be found guilty, she will also miss the Titans' Round 7 clash at home against the Dragons alongside this weekend's showdown against the Sharks.
No plea has been submitted at this time.

items.body_excerpt:
Tom Dearden has shut down chatter the North Queensland star would tear up his contract and move to Sydney in a fiery press conference in Townsville.
The rugby league rumour mill ignited when the Cowboys co-captain’s partner – Sydney business owner Millie Olliver – revealed the pair were expecting their first child .
Among those suggestions were the Queensland Maroons halfback would seek an early release from his lucrative five-year deal which expires at the end of 2029.
Tom Dearden is closing in on a return from injury. Getty Images
But Dearden, fronting reporters despite remaining sidelined through injury, dispelled the theory and said he was fed up with the questions aimed at his family.
“I don’t feel like I should have to get up here and explain myself against speculation because it’s just been a whole lot of nonsense. I’ve got my private life with a partner who’s pregnant, and I’d like for that to all be kept private,” Dearden said.
“It’s had an impact on the private life. When there’s speculation going around like that, you know that people are reading that, and it gives them questions to ask, and you always have to answer to people – my partner has had to do the same as well.
“The private life part is private for a reason, and I just think it’s a bit disappointing my partner and family has had to deal with a lot of questions because of speculation that has gone around in the media.
“There have been no suggestions or no thinking about not being committed to the Cowboys. I’m not recommitting … I’ve always been committed to the Cowboys.”
Dearden has endured an injury-riddled campaign, having undergone surgery on a syndesmosis issue which robbed him of a State of Origin appearance — one which would have given him the chance to defend his Wally Lewis Medal.
He managed just one game on his comeback – scoring a try and setting up another in the Cowboys’ loss to the Dolphins – before being sidelined again with a muscle tear in his shin.
In his absence, North Queensland secured a hard-fought triumph of the Broncos before suffering the worst defeat in their history against the Roosters – an 82-12 capitulation which coach Todd Payten described as their “darkest day”.
The loss leaves the club teetering on the brink of the finals’ wilderness, currently sitting in ninth but with a bye up their sleeve, which Dearden revealed was his intended comeback date.
“It’s actually tracking pretty well, I’ve hopefully only got a few more weeks and the shin is starting to feel pretty good,” Dearden said.
“I’m hoping to be back after the bye, I think that’s about three or four weeks away now, and that’ll give it enough time for this injury to heal. I want to make sure I’m right before I come back.”

items.body_excerpt:
Presented By
As it happened: Ruthless Roosters roast Cowboys
The Cowboys were back at home again in Round 22 and were keen to make a statement against one of the competition heavyweights, the Roosters.
Instead, they were handed a record defeat, with the huge 82-12 score conceded putting doubt on their spot in the top eight.
The fast-finishing Bulldogs are now a chance of jumping into their place if they can defeat the Storm on Friday night.
The Roosters continued their winning run at Queensland Country Bank Stadium, and have now won five from five.
Captain James Tedesco didn't play the second half and was seen with ice on his left ankle, but the club did not seem too concerned about any long-term issue.
Follow all the action from Round 22 of the NRL Telstra Premiership on NRL.com's live blog.
Cowboys v Roosters at Queensland Country Bank Stadium
Match: Cowboys v Roosters
Round 22 - Round 22 - Thursday 30 Jul
home Team
Cowboys
9th Position
away Team
Roosters

Venue: Queensland Country Bank Stadium, Townsville
Press conferences
Cowboys: Round 22
Roosters: Round 22
Points, points, points: Mark Nawaqanitawase and Sam Walker both scored hat-tricks, James Tedesco scored a double playing only in the first half and Hugo Savala also had a double. Walker also kicked 12 conversions. The Roosters made a statement against a top eight contender and are challenging for the minor premiership.
Full-time: An utterly devastating performance by the Roosters who have destroyed the Cowboys at home and could have stuck a knife in their top eight standing with their huge 82-12 victory. It was the most points conceded in a game for 91 years - the first time a team has scored 80 points since 1935. The Roosters were dominant in all facets - they had 64 percent of the possession with a 90 percent completion rate with 43/39. The Cowboys missed 42 tackles compared to 19 from the Roosters and in the metres run, the Sydney-siders produced almost double, pumping out 2275 compared to 1154 for North Queensland.
From the field: Reuben Cotter
78th min: The Roosters have hit 80 points. It's been one way traffic - bar two tries to the Cowboys, one in each half - and this time it is Cody Ramsey who scores the try. Walker kicks another conversion - his 12th of the night. Roosters are up 82-12 .
78th min: After giving up a 'downtown' penalty to carry the Roosters all the way back into their attacking half, the Cowboys can't hold out the visitors, with Hugo Savala going through a gap at the line created from a Walker dummy to get his second. Walker converts again for a huge 76-12 lead.
72nd min: It's just one of those nights they'd like to forget for the Cowboys - but one to savour for the Roosters. The play ends up in a hat-trick for Sam Walker , but it was shaping to be a try for the home side on the other end of the field. Instead, a pass to Drinkwater with the try-line begging proved too hard to handle, with Ramsey picking up the ball and sprinting away. The Cowboys chase, so the ball goes back inside to Walker who gets in under the posts. Walker is back on the conversion and it's 70-12 .
Sam Walker 3rd Try
71st min: A captain's challenge from the Roosters is successful - but they instead give up a penalty.
68th min: A hat-trick for Mark Nawaqanitawase who shows his strength to get the ball down despite the attention of four Cowboys defenders who can't drag him down. Cody Ramsey has taken over the kicking duties and slots it from the right sideline for a 64-12 lead.
62nd min: More points for the Roosters off a scrum play 10m out from their attacking line, gained from a double knock on call. They set the scrum to the right with a 3-3 split and Rob Toia runs his way around to score through a gaping hole. Sam Walker slots another one from in front and it's 58-12 .
Robert Toia Try
